clue.text: Cover put around album not working? It's beyond remedy

indicators.note: put around says the cover goes round the outside of the shuffled album letters

parts.note: to cover something against loss is to insure it

indicators.note: working means fermenting or being worked over, so the letters of the preceding words are reshaped

explanation.surface: A grumble about a broken album whose sleeve was replaced: some faults simply cannot be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not working' looks like a description of the album, but 'not' belongs to the fodder and only 'working' signals the rearrangement. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle that cannot be overcome or a problem past fixing is, in synonym terms, impossible to surmount.

clue.text: Hold reason for beheading number of revolutionaries

parts.note: to intern is to hold someone in detention

indicators.note: beheading means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a rationale is a reason

explanation.surface: Detaining people as a pretext to behead a crowd of revolutionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a count but is a song; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Internationale is the socialist anthem, a song sung by revolutionaries.

clue.text: Turned down drive with little room to reverse

parts.note: to spur is to drive on

indicators.note: to reverse means the letters are written backwards

parts.note: a den is a small private room

explanation.surface: Someone refused a driveway with too little space to reverse a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurned means rejected or refused with contempt.

clue.text: Transported again after theatre show

indicators.note: after says the second piece comes after the theatre

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
re-sent means dispatched again

explanation.surface: People carried off once more after a theatre performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transported' suggests delight, but read as re-sent, shipped once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something is to depict or portray it, exhibit it.

clue.text: Main inhabitant has work after a month

indicators.note: after puts the work following the month

parts.note: Oct. is October
an opus is a musical work

explanation.surface: A seaside resident gets work some months later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, the main, not chief.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus lives in the ocean, a sea creature with eight arms.

clue.text: Gent's clothing down, on the game

parts.note: to neck a drink is to down it
a tie is a game, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A gentleman stripped and down on his luck, working as a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the game' suggests prostitution; 'on' is a link. A cup tie is a knockout match in British football.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is a piece of menswear worn around the collar.

clue.text: Recalling medic for a mission

parts.note: à la means in the style of, recalling something
MO is medical officer

explanation.surface: A doctor called back to serve on a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalling' suggests turning back, but means reminiscent of; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo in Texas was a Spanish mission, famous for the 1836 siege.

clue.text: Charged after having departed Roman site

indicators.note: after having puts the charging piece following the other

parts.note: the late are the departed, the dead
to charge is to run at something

explanation.surface: Someone charged after leaving a Roman location.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lateran is a district of Rome holding the papal basilica of St John.

clue.text: Knackered wife to relax with swimmer's sport

parts.note: all in is British slang for exhausted
w is wife in genealogies
to rest is to relax
a ling is a fish

explanation.surface: An exhausted wife goes off to relax with a swimmer's sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' is a fish; 'Knackered' is British for worn out. 'to' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: All-in wrestling is a freestyle form of grappling with few holds barred.

clue.text: Behind blocking name of offensive broadcast

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the middle of the other piece, obstructing it

parts.note: the Tet Offensive of 1968 in the Vietnam War
the rump is one's behind, the backside

explanation.surface: Someone's backside gets in the way of an offensive broadcast, perhaps on a TV screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective describing the broadcast, but it is the Tet Offensive; 'broadcast' is a verb, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet news is to proclaim it loudly far and wide, as a broadcaster spreads it.

clue.text: Things one has to discuss by phone

definitions.note: plural, where the answer is singular, though it can be used collectively for possessions

parts.note: to chat is to discuss informally
Tel. is the abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: A list of things a person must talk over on the telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plural while the answer is singular; the bloggers noted the mismatch, which is defensible only reading the word collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: A chattel is a piece of movable personal property, an item someone owns.

clue.text: Foreign royal smuggled drug repeatedly

parts.note: to run contraband is to smuggle it, so ran is smuggled

indicators.note: repeatedly says the drug letter appears twice in a row

parts.note: E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A foreign princess was caught smuggling drugs again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranee is the wife of a rajah, or a Hindu queen, so a royal from abroad.

clue.text: Mixture to decant into pan, covering for ravioli

indicators.note: into says the pouring goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a pot is a cooking pan

indicators.note: the covering of a word is its outside letters, first and last

parts.note: to decant wine is to pour it out

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: decant into the pan the sauce that will cover the ravioli.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering for ravioli' means the word's outside letters, not a sauce; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a medley or miscellany, a jumble of assorted items.

clue.text: Notice incompletely attired earl, one getting a talking-to?

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper

indicators.note: incompletely says the last letter of the synonym is cut off

parts.note: attired means dressed

explanation.surface: A notice about a half-dressed earl, who will surely be told off.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'talking-to' suggests a scolding, but the definition simply means someone spoken to; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The addressee is the person a letter or speech is directed at, so they receive the talk.

clue.text: Power of great city is ebbing

indicators.note: ebbing means flowing back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the Great Wen is Cobbett's nickname for London; a wen is a cyst

explanation.surface: The might of a great city is in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the great wen' is an old disparaging nickname for London, so WEN stands for a great city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew is a tendon, and by extension muscular strength or force.

clue.text: Rocky base affected roads in coastal regions

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so these letters wobble into a new order
affected means disturbed or altered, so these letters are reworked too

explanation.surface: A rocky foundation has damaged roads along the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaboards are the stretches of land bordering the sea, coastlines.

clue.text: Some abstaining, others in bar

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: In the pub, some people are on the wagon while others are drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is a bar of metal; 'in bar' means cast in that form.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold cast as a solid block or bar is held in that shape, the form of bullion.

clue.text: Coaching cooking, tossing out a dish

indicators.note: cooking means messing with, so the letters are rearranged
tossing out says a letter is thrown out of the mix

explanation.surface: A cookery coach tossing ingredients into a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: COACHING with A removed, then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are Italian dumplings, served as a dish.

clue.text: Flee or fly in traveller's seat

indicators.note: in says the fly sits inside the seat

parts.note: a rider travels sitting in a saddle
a ked is a wingless fly, the sheep ked

explanation.surface: A traveller with a fly in the saddle wants to run or fly off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like a synonym of 'Flee', but it is the insect KED; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To skedaddle is a jocular word for running away hastily.

clue.text: Swimming, Phelps maintains top speed in hard journey

indicators.note: maintains means keeps hold of, so the speed sits inside
swimming means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: c is the speed of light, the fastest possible

explanation.surface: Michael Phelps keeps his top speed through an exhausting swim.
explanation.definitionFit: A schlep is a tedious, arduous trek, Yiddish in origin.

clue.text: Put plainly, any number tucking into cake

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside

parts.note: an éclair is a pastry
n denotes any number in algebra

explanation.surface: A greedy eater bluntly confesses to tucking into a lot of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: En clair means in plain language, not in code.

clue.text: Horseman and I went off to the north

indicators.note: to the north means upward, reversing the letters in a down clue

parts.note: food that went off rotted

explanation.surface: A rider and I headed off northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went off' suggests left, but means decayed; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankie Dettori is a famous jockey who rides racehorses.

clue.text: Frantically on the go, I see, like the Houses of Parliament

indicators.note: something done frantically is wild and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letter C is named 'see', a common crossword equivalence

explanation.surface: Someone frantically busy reporting what they see, as busy as Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: ON THE GO rearranged gives NEOGOTH; 'I see' then supplies I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: The Palace of Westminster was rebuilt in the Victorian Gothic Revival style, a pointed-arch medieval manner.

clue.text: Primate called round to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with says the round letter goes at the front

parts.note: O is round in shape
rang means called by phone

explanation.surface: An ape phoned around at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An orang is short for orang-utan, a great ape.

clue.text: Retrograde and the like in religious book group

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the book

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the letters run reversed

parts.note: etc. is et cetera, and the like

explanation.surface: A group reading a religious book, and other such backward stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, especially eight musicians.

clue.text: What mums do at night, bored by routine

indicators.note: bored by means pierced, with the routine drilled into the middle

parts.note: late means at a late hour, night-time
an act is a performer's routine

explanation.surface: Mothers up late feeding babies, bored stiff by the routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lactating mothers produce milk to feed their babies, a verb for that action.

clue.text: Time for fooling around carnival city, theoretically

indicators.note: around says the time goes round the city

parts.note: April 1, written Apr 1, is April Fools' Day
Rio de Janeiro is famous for its carnival

explanation.surface: Fooling about at Rio's carnival, in theory a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: April 1 is April Fools' Day; the numeral 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori reasoning works from theory or deduction rather than observation or experience.

clue.text: Thus drinking in break, one leaves wine cocktail

indicators.note: drinking says one piece takes the others inside it

parts.note: so means thus
a gap is a break

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so one is taken out of the wine

parts.note: Riesling is a white wine grape and wine
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Drinking during a break, then leaving the wine for a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Singapore sling is a gin-based cocktail first mixed at the Raffles Hotel.
